name: Lakshmi Discovers Likely Schemes From One Sentence
description: A parent describes her daughter's situation in one short sentence, answers only 2–4 follow-up questions, and sees schemes grouped as Likely eligible, May qualify, or Not currently eligible.

steps.description: Lakshmi opens HaqPath, chooses English or the regional language, and reads the trust statement before continuing.

business_rules.name: language_choice_sets_session_language
business_rules.description: The language Lakshmi picks on the welcome screen (English or the regional language) becomes the display language for every later step in the session.
triggers: Lakshmi taps English or the regional language on the welcome screen
side_effects: All following screens, rules text, and read-aloud output use the chosen language
The choice is held for the current session only and is not saved to a Profile record at this step
error_handling: If the chosen language's translations are missing for a screen, that screen shows English text and the language toggle stays visible
If no language is selected, Continue stays disabled and the page asks Lakshmi to choose one

business_rules.name: trust_statement_must_be_acknowledged_before_continue
business_rules.description: The Continue action stays locked until Lakshmi has been shown the full trust statement and has acknowledged it (welcome screen sequence: language selected → trust statement viewed → acknowledged → Continue enabled).
triggers: Lakshmi scrolls to the end of the trust statement or taps the acknowledgment control
Lakshmi attempts to tap Continue before acknowledging
side_effects: Continue becomes active and Lakshmi moves to the 'Tell us about your situation' screen
The acknowledgment is held for the session and is not saved as a stored record at this step
error_handling: If Lakshmi taps Continue before acknowledging, Continue does not proceed and the trust statement is brought into view with a short prompt
If the trust statement fails to load, the page shows the full disclaimer text inline so the acknowledgment can still happen

business_rules.name: trust_statement_uses_required_disclaimer_wording
business_rules.description: The welcome trust statement includes the required disclaimer 'HaqPath provides guidance based on published rules. Final eligibility is decided by the relevant authority.' and uses no guaranteed or approval language.
triggers: The welcome screen renders in either language
side_effects: The disclaimer appears on the welcome screen in the selected language, in the same wording in both languages
The statement states that HaqPath uses fictional or demo data where applicable
error_handling: If the translated disclaimer is unavailable, the English wording is shown alongside the regional label rather than omitting the disclaimer

business_rules.name: welcome_screen_collects_no_personal_data
business_rules.description: The welcome screen collects no personal identifiers, bank details, document scans, or sensitive identity data; only the language choice and the trust acknowledgment are captured.
triggers: Lakshmi is on the welcome screen
side_effects: No Profile values are created or changed on this screen
error_handling: If any field requesting sensitive data is found on this screen, it is removed before release

business_rules.name: welcome_screen_checks_language_toggle_availability
business_rules.description: The language toggle remains available on the welcome screen so Lakshmi can switch between English and the regional language before acknowledging the trust statement.
triggers: Lakshmi taps the language toggle after first choosing a language
side_effects: The welcome screen and trust statement re-render in the newly selected language without losing the acknowledgment state
error_handling: If switching language fails, the previous language stays active and a short message says the switch did not work

validation_rules.description: Lakshmi must choose either English or the regional language before continuing.
validation_rules.error_message: Please choose a language to continue. / कृपया आगे बढ़ने के लिए भाषा चुनें।

validation_rules.description: The language value must be one of the two supported options, English or the regional language.
validation_rules.error_message: This language is not available yet. Please choose English or the regional language.

validation_rules.description: Lakshmi must acknowledge the trust statement (by scrolling to its end or tapping 'I understand') before continuing.
validation_rules.error_message: Please read and confirm the trust statement before continuing. / आगे बढ़ने से पहले कृपया विश्वास विवरण पढ़कर पुष्टि करें।

steps.description: Lakshmi types one short sentence about her daughter's class, school type, and household income in plain language.

business_rules.name: extract_profile_from_one_sentence
business_rules.description: The one-sentence situation is sent to OpenAI, which extracts class level, institution type, and household income into Profile fields, while the rules engine alone decides eligibility later.
triggers: Lakshmi submits her one-sentence description of her daughter's class, school type, and household income
Lakshmi finishes speaking and the voice transcript is ready to submit
side_effects: Profile.raw_situation_text is saved as typed or transcribed
Profile.class_level, Profile.institution_type, and Profile.annual_household_income are filled only where the sentence clearly states them
Any field the sentence does not clearly state is left empty, not guessed
error_handling: OpenAI extraction fails or times out: keep Profile.raw_situation_text, leave all extracted fields empty, and ask Lakshmi to answer the follow-up questions directly
OpenAI returns a value outside the allowed set (for example class 9): discard that value and treat the field as unanswered
The sentence is in the regional language: OpenAI translates it for extraction, but Profile.raw_situation_text keeps the original wording

business_rules.name: institution_type_must_use_closed_set
business_rules.description: Profile.institution_type can only be government, government_aided, private, or unknown, because each scheme rule matches against those exact values.
triggers: Extraction returns an institution description from the sentence
Lakshmi later changes the institution type on the follow-up question
side_effects: Profile.institution_type is stored as one of the four allowed values
Profile.institution_type set to unknown causes the matching step to classify affected schemes as May qualify with the institution type listed as needing confirmation
error_handling: Wording like 'convent' or 'public school' cannot be mapped confidently: set institution_type to unknown and ask one follow-up question
An unrecognised value is rejected and the follow-up question is shown again

business_rules.name: class_level_limited_to_class_11_or_12
business_rules.description: Profile.class_level must be 11 or 12; any other class moves the profile out of scope and the product says so respectfully.
triggers: Extraction returns a class level from the sentence
Lakshmi answers the class follow-up question
side_effects: Profile.class_level is stored as 11 or 12 when it is in scope
When Profile.class_level is outside 11 or 12, the flow shows an out-of-scope message and does not run scheme matching
error_handling: A class outside 11 to 12 is accepted as a profile but shown as out of scope with a plain explanation that HaqPath currently covers Classes 11 and 12
A class value that cannot be read is treated as unanswered and asked again

business_rules.name: income_stored_as_annual_amount_only
business_rules.description: Profile.annual_household_income stores only a yearly rupee amount or band as stated, and the rules engine compares it with each scheme's maximum income threshold.
triggers: Extraction returns an income phrase such as 'low income' or 'about 2 lakh a year' from the sentence
Lakshmi answers the income follow-up question
side_effects: Profile.annual_household_income is stored as an annual amount when stated, or as a declared band such as below 2.5 lakh when only a band is given
A vague phrase such as 'low income' leaves the amount empty and marks income as needing confirmation on matched schemes
error_handling: A vague income phrase does not map to an amount: leave Profile.annual_household_income empty and ask one follow-up question with clear band options
An income figure that is implausibly large or negative is rejected and the question is asked again

business_rules.name: no_sensitive_identity_data_stored
business_rules.description: Any Aadhaar-like number, bank detail, or document reference in the sentence is removed before saving, and Profile never stores a name, phone number, or identity number.
triggers: Lakshmi types or speaks a number or detail that looks like an identity or bank identifier
Profile is created or updated from the intake sentence
side_effects: Matching identifiers are replaced with a redaction marker in Profile.raw_situation_text before it is saved to Upstash
Lakshmi sees a short notice that HaqPath does not need ID or bank numbers
error_handling: A 12-digit number is detected: it is redacted, the sentence is not rejected, and the notice is shown
Stored text cannot be sanitised with confidence: Profile.raw_situation_text is not saved and Lakshmi is asked to rephrase without numbers

business_rules.name: unanswered_fields_drive_next_question
business_rules.description: After extraction, the highest-value missing Profile field is asked next, and optional questions can be skipped without blocking the results.
triggers: Extraction completes and at least one of class_level, institution_type, or annual_household_income is empty
Lakshmi skips an optional follow-up question
side_effects: Profile records which fields are still unanswered so the follow-up flow shows only those
Skipped fields stay empty and the matched schemes list them under what still needs verification
error_handling: All three fields are answered: no follow-up question is asked and the flow moves on
Lakshmi skips every optional question: results still appear, with unanswered rules shown as May qualify

business_rules.name: anonymous_profile_saved_to_upstash
business_rules.description: Each intake creates or updates an anonymous Profile keyed by a session identifier and stored in Upstash, so the demo works with fictional personas and no account is required.
triggers: Lakshmi submits the intake sentence for the first time in a session
Lakshmi edits a profile answer during the flow
side_effects: A Profile record is written to Upstash keyed by an anonymous session identifier
Matching results are recalculated from the saved Profile on the next screen
error_handling: Upstash is unreachable: keep the Profile in the browser session and show a notice that progress will not be saved
A demo persona is selected: its preloaded Profile is used instead of creating a new one

validation_rules.description: The situation sentence must not be empty after trimming spaces.
validation_rules.error_message: Please tell us a little about your situation in one sentence.

validation_rules.description: The situation sentence must be between 5 and 300 characters.
validation_rules.error_message: Please keep your message between 5 and 300 characters. Short sentences work best.

validation_rules.description: The sentence must not contain a 12-digit number (Aadhaar-like) or a bank account-like number of 9 to 18 digits; such numbers are redacted before saving.
validation_rules.error_message: Please do not type ID or bank numbers. HaqPath does not need them. Tell us about your daughter's class, school type, and income instead.

steps.description: The app sends the sentence to OpenAI, which only extracts structured profile fields (class level, institution type, state, income band) and returns them with a confidence flag. Deterministic rules are not decided here.

business_rules.name: ai_extracts_profile_fields_only
business_rules.description: OpenAI only reads the user's sentence and returns class level, institution type, state, and income band with a confidence flag for each; it never decides eligibility.
triggers: User submits the one-sentence description on the 'Tell us about your situation' screen
IntakeRoute receives the sentence and calls OpenAI for extraction
side_effects: Extracted values and their confidence flags are written to the Profile in Upstash
No eligibility result is produced at this step; EligibilityResult is untouched until the deterministic rules run later
error_handling: OpenAI returns a response that is not valid structured JSON: discard the response, leave all four fields empty, and ask the user the follow-up questions for each field
OpenAI returns a verdict or eligibility text instead of extracted fields: ignore everything except the four allowed fields
OpenAI request times out or fails: continue with an empty Profile and show the first follow-up question

business_rules.name: low_confidence_extraction_treated_as_unknown
business_rules.description: An extracted field whose confidence flag is 'low' is stored as unknown rather than as a value, so it is asked again in the follow-up questions.
triggers: OpenAI returns a field with a low confidence flag
Extraction result is saved to the Profile
side_effects: The low-confidence field is left empty in the Profile
The field is queued as the next highest-value follow-up question
error_handling: Confidence flag is missing for a field: treat it as low confidence
All four fields are low confidence: the user is asked all four follow-up questions, but the flow still continues

business_rules.name: extracted_values_must_match_allowed_set
business_rules.description: An extracted value is accepted only if it belongs to the allowed set for its field, such as class levels 11 or 12, the defined institution types, the configured state, and the defined income bands.
triggers: OpenAI returns a value for any of the four profile fields
Extraction result is validated before it is saved
side_effects: Values outside the allowed set are dropped and the field is left empty
Dropped values are queued as follow-up questions
error_handling: Class level is 'Class 10' or 'college': drop it, since this product covers only Classes 11 to 12
State is outside the configured state: store the value as given for the out-of-scope check, do not match it to the scheme catalogue here
Income band is a rupee amount rather than a band: map it to the band only if it fits exactly; otherwise leave it empty

business_rules.name: user_confirmed_answers_override_extraction
business_rules.description: A profile field the user has explicitly confirmed or answered is never overwritten by a later AI extraction.
triggers: User answers a follow-up question or edits a value on the screen
A later sentence is sent to IntakeRoute and extraction returns a different value for the same field
side_effects: The confirmed value stays in the Profile
The AI value for that field is discarded
error_handling: Extraction conflicts with a confirmed value: keep the confirmed value and record that the new sentence was not applied to that field

business_rules.name: sentence_stripped_of_identifiers_before_ai
business_rules.description: Before the sentence is sent to OpenAI, any number that looks like an Aadhaar or other identity number is removed, and the raw sentence is not stored in the Profile.
triggers: User submits a sentence that contains a 12-digit number or similar identifier
IntakeRoute prepares the sentence for OpenAI
side_effects: The identifier is removed from the text sent to OpenAI
The user is told that identity numbers are not needed and were not saved
error_handling: Identifier-like number detected: strip it and continue with the rest of the sentence
Stripping leaves the sentence empty: ask the user to describe their situation without numbers

validation_rules.description: The description sentence cannot be empty or only spaces.
validation_rules.error_message: Please tell us a little about your situation, for example: My daughter is in Class 11 at a government college.

validation_rules.description: The description sentence is between 3 and 300 characters.
validation_rules.error_message: Please keep your description short, under 300 characters. One or two sentences is enough.

validation_rules.description: The sentence cannot contain a 12-digit number, which could be an Aadhaar number.
validation_rules.error_message: Please do not type ID numbers such as Aadhaar. HaqPath does not need them.

steps.description: Lakshmi sees the highest-value missing question first, such as the annual household income band, and can answer or skip optional questions.

business_rules.name: highest_value_unanswered_question_shown_first
business_rules.description: The follow-up flow shows the unanswered question that would change the most scheme results, which is the annual household income band whenever it is still missing, then institution type, then class level.
triggers: Lakshmi reaches the follow-up step after the first sentence is processed
Lakshmi answers or skips a question and the flow advances
side_effects: The next question displayed is the highest-value unanswered question for Profile
Questions already answered from the first sentence are not asked again
The flow ends once two to four questions are answered or skipped, moving Lakshmi to the results screen
error_handling: If Profile.annual_household_income_band is missing and no scheme rule depends on it, the flow skips to the next unanswered question
If all high-value questions are already answered, the flow ends and results are shown without further questions
If the profile cannot be loaded, Lakshmi sees a plain message and can retry without losing earlier answers

business_rules.name: optional_questions_can_be_skipped_and_mark_results_for_verification
business_rules.description: Lakshmi can skip any optional follow-up question, and each skipped answer is recorded on Profile so that schemes depending on it are shown as may qualify rather than likely eligible (unanswered → skipped, with the answer still treated as unknown).
triggers: Lakshmi taps the skip control on an optional follow-up question
side_effects: The question key is added to Profile.skipped_questions
EligibilityResult.status for schemes that depend on the skipped answer becomes may_qualify
The skipped requirement is listed in EligibilityResult.unverified_requirements with a plain note that it still needs confirming
The flow advances to the next question without showing an error
error_handling: If a question is marked required for a scheme that Lakshmi has already ruled out, skipping it does not change that result
If the skip is recorded but the save fails, the question is shown again with a message asking Lakshmi to try once more

business_rules.name: income_answer_immediately_recalculates_scheme_status
business_rules.description: Each answered question is saved to Profile and compared with the income ceiling in EligibilityRule so that a household income above the scheme limit moves that scheme to not currently eligible (answered → evaluated → result status updated).
triggers: Lakshmi selects an annual household income band
Lakshmi selects an institution type or class level
side_effects: Profile.annual_household_income_band is saved
EligibilityResult.status is recalculated for every Scheme with a rule that uses income
Schemes whose income ceiling is exceeded get EligibilityResult.status set to not_currently_eligible with a plain explanation in EligibilityResult.why_not_fit
Schemes that now pass the income check but still have open requirements are set to may_qualify
error_handling: If the selected income band cannot be mapped to a numeric value, the answer is stored but no scheme is excluded on income and the result is marked may_qualify
If recalculation fails, the previous results remain visible with a note that they are being refreshed

validation_rules.description: An income band must be selected from the defined list, or the question must be explicitly skipped.
validation_rules.error_message: Choose your yearly household income range, or tap Skip to answer later.

validation_rules.description: Institution type must be one of government, government_aided, or private, or the question must be explicitly skipped.
validation_rules.error_message: Choose the type of school or college your child attends, or tap Skip.

validation_rules.description: Class level must be 11 or 12 to match the scope of the catalogue.
validation_rules.error_message: Choose Class 11 or Class 12.

steps.description: The app loads the scheme catalogue and editable eligibility rules from Upstash and evaluates each rule deterministically against the profile.

business_rules.name: eligibility_decided_only_by_stored_rules
business_rules.description: Every EligibilityResult is produced by evaluating the stored EligibilityRule conditions against the Profile, and no AI model or generated text decides whether a scheme matches.
triggers: A results request arrives for a Profile
The results screen loads after the follow-up questions are answered
side_effects: One EligibilityResult is created for each active Scheme, recording its status and the criteria behind it
No AI-generated text is stored as an eligibility decision
error_handling: If a rule cannot be parsed or evaluated, its scheme is excluded from results and the failure is logged, and the other schemes still return
If the rule set is empty, the response returns no results with a message that the catalogue is being updated

business_rules.name: three_outcome_classification
business_rules.description: Each EligibilityResult takes exactly one status in this order of precedence: not currently eligible when any hard criterion fails, may qualify when criteria are unknown but none fail, and likely eligible when every criterion is confirmed.
triggers: Each scheme is evaluated against the Profile during a results request
side_effects: EligibilityResult.status is set to likely_eligible, may_qualify, or not_currently_eligible
The results screen groups schemes by this status
error_handling: A criterion with no Profile value is marked unverified and does not count as a failure
A Profile with conflicting values, such as a class level outside 11 to 12, is flagged for confirmation rather than rejected

business_rules.name: every_result_records_its_reasons
business_rules.description: Each EligibilityResult stores its matched, unverified, and failed criteria so the app can show why a scheme may fit, what still needs checking, and why it may not fit.
triggers: An EligibilityResult is written for a scheme
side_effects: The scheme detail screen can show the exact rule and the Profile value that met or missed it
The 'What changes my result?' feature can name the criterion that changed
error_handling: A result with no recorded criteria is not shown, because it could not be explained

business_rules.name: unverified_criteria_never_reject
business_rules.description: A Profile value that is missing or unknown moves a scheme to may qualify with that criterion listed for confirmation, and it never moves the scheme to not currently eligible.
triggers: A Profile field needed by an EligibilityRule is empty or was skipped by the user
side_effects: EligibilityResult.status becomes may_qualify when no other criterion fails
The scheme detail screen lists the missing item as something to verify with the authority
error_handling: If a skipped optional question blocks a criterion, the scheme is kept as may_qualify rather than dropped

business_rules.name: state_and_class_level_are_hard_criteria
business_rules.description: A scheme is not currently eligible when Profile.state is not in EligibilityRule.state or Profile.class_level is not in EligibilityRule.class_levels.
triggers: Profile.state or Profile.class_level is compared against an EligibilityRule during evaluation
side_effects: EligibilityResult.status becomes not_currently_eligible
The failed criterion is recorded with the Profile value and the rule value
error_handling: If Profile.state is unknown, the state criterion is treated as unverified, not failed

business_rules.name: income_and_institution_thresholds_applied_as_written
business_rules.description: A scheme is not currently eligible when Profile.annual_household_income is above EligibilityRule.max_annual_income or when Profile.institution_type is not in EligibilityRule.institution_types.
triggers: Profile.institution_type or Profile.annual_household_income changes and the results are recalculated
A results request is evaluated against the EligibilityRule thresholds
side_effects: A scheme that previously showed as may_qualify or likely_eligible can move to not_currently_eligible
The changed criterion is available to the 'What changes my result?' screen
error_handling: A non-numeric income value is treated as unverified, not as zero

business_rules.name: only_verified_active_schemes_are_evaluated
business_rules.description: Only Scheme records with is_active set to true, an official_url, and a last_verified_at date are evaluated, and any scheme whose deadline has passed is marked as closed rather than dropped.
triggers: The catalogue is loaded from Upstash at the start of a results request
side_effects: Schemes missing a source link or verification date are left out of results
Schemes past their deadline show as closed, with the deadline date visible
error_handling: A scheme without last_verified_at is excluded and the exclusion is logged for the content team
A deadline that cannot be parsed is shown as deadline to be confirmed

business_rules.name: upstash_outage_falls_back_to_bundled_catalogue
business_rules.description: If Upstash cannot be reached, the Scheme and EligibilityRule data is served from the bundled, preloaded fictional catalogue so the demo still produces results.
triggers: A read from Upstash fails or times out during a results request
side_effects: Results are computed from the bundled catalogue
The results response is marked as coming from the offline catalogue so the UI can show that status
error_handling: If the bundled catalogue is also unavailable, the response returns an error message asking the user to try again later, not an empty result list

business_rules.name: results_are_recomputed_not_reused
business_rules.description: EligibilityResult records are recalculated from the current Profile on every results request, so a changed answer always changes the output.
triggers: Profile.institution_type, Profile.class_level, Profile.state, Profile.annual_household_income, or Profile.category is changed
The user returns to the results screen after editing an answer
side_effects: EligibilityResult.evaluated_at is updated
The results list reflects the new status for each affected scheme
error_handling: If a prior EligibilityResult cannot be replaced, the new result is still returned and the old one is marked superseded

steps.description: Lakshmi sees the results grouped as Likely eligible, May qualify, and Not currently eligible, each with a short respectful reason and the trust disclaimer.

business_rules.name: results_grouped_into_three_statuses
business_rules.description: Every scheme is placed in exactly one of three groups on the results page: likely_eligible, may_qualify, or not_currently_eligible, shown in that order.
triggers: Lakshmi finishes the follow-up questions and the results page loads
Lakshmi changes a profile answer and the results page is recalculated
side_effects: Each scheme card appears under its group heading: Likely eligible, May qualify, or Not currently eligible
An empty group shows a short note saying no schemes fall in that group for now, instead of disappearing silently
error_handling: If a scheme has no EligibilityResult for the current Profile, it is not shown and the page notes that some schemes could not be checked yet
If an EligibilityResult has a status outside the three allowed values, it is treated as may_qualify and the issue is logged for review

business_rules.name: results_use_only_approved_status_language
business_rules.description: Result group labels and card text use only the wording Likely eligible, May qualify, and Not currently eligible, and never use words such as approved, guaranteed, rejected, or sure.
triggers: The results page renders any group heading, card, or summary line
side_effects: Group headings and card badges display the mapped plain-language label for each EligibilityResult.status
Reason text stored on EligibilityResult is checked for banned words before it is shown
error_handling: If a stored reason_text contains a banned word such as approved or guaranteed, the card shows a generic safe reason and the record is flagged for content review

business_rules.name: every_result_shows_respectful_reason
business_rules.description: Each scheme card shows one short, respectful reason in simple language that explains its group, drawn from the rules that were met, still need confirmation, or were not met.
triggers: A scheme card is rendered on the results page
side_effects: Likely eligible cards show the main reason it fits
May qualify cards name the one or more details that need confirmation
Not currently eligible cards name the single most important unmet condition in gentle wording, without blaming the family
error_handling: If reason_text is empty, the card falls back to the Scheme.plain_language_explanation so the card never appears blank
If unmet_rule_ids references a rule that no longer exists, the card shows a general reason and the mismatch is logged

business_rules.name: not_currently_eligible_explains_the_unmet_condition
business_rules.description: A scheme is placed in not_currently_eligible only when at least one required rule is definitively unmet, and its reason names that unmet condition.
triggers: The matching run finishes and marks a scheme as failing a required rule
side_effects: The scheme card shows the unmet condition in respectful wording
The card keeps the official source link so the family can still check the rule themselves
error_handling: If a rule cannot be evaluated because a profile answer is missing, the scheme goes to may_qualify rather than not_currently_eligible
If unmet_rule_ids is empty but status is not_currently_eligible, the status is corrected to may_qualify and logged

business_rules.name: unconfirmed_details_keep_scheme_in_may_qualify
business_rules.description: A scheme is placed in may_qualify when no required rule is definitively unmet but one or more rules still need confirmation, and the card lists those details.
triggers: The matching run finishes with unanswered or unverified rule inputs for a scheme
side_effects: The card shows a What we still need to verify list drawn from the unconfirmed rules
The family sees that confirming those details could move the scheme to likely_eligible
error_handling: If there are more than three unconfirmed details, the card shows the first three and a line saying more details are listed on the scheme page

business_rules.name: likely_eligible_requires_all_required_rules_met
business_rules.description: A scheme is placed in likely_eligible only when every required rule is met and no required rule is unconfirmed or unmet.
triggers: The matching run finishes for a scheme whose required rules have all been satisfied
side_effects: The card appears in the Likely eligible group with a why it may fit summary
The card still shows the official source and verification date, and the disclaimer stays visible on the page
error_handling: If a likely_eligible result has any entry in unconfirmed_rule_ids, the status is downgraded to may_qualify before rendering

business_rules.name: expired_deadline_moves_scheme_to_not_currently_eligible
business_rules.description: A scheme whose Scheme.deadline has passed is placed in not_currently_eligible with the reason that the application window has closed, regardless of other rule results.
triggers: The results page is loaded on a date after a scheme's deadline
side_effects: The card shows that the application window has closed and points to the official source for the next cycle
The scheme no longer appears in likely_eligible or may_qualify for that day
error_handling: If Scheme.deadline is missing, the deadline rule is skipped and the card notes that the deadline needs checking on the official page

business_rules.name: every_result_shows_official_source_and_verification_date
business_rules.description: Every scheme card on the results page shows its official source link and the Last verified on date taken from the scheme record.
triggers: A scheme card is rendered in any group
side_effects: A visible Last verified on date appears on each card
The official source link opens the government page for that scheme
error_handling: If official_url is missing, the card is not shown in any group and the scheme is flagged as incomplete in the dataset
If last_verified_at is older than the agreed review window, the card shows a note that the information should be checked on the official page

business_rules.name: disclaimer_shown_on_every_results_view
business_rules.description: The trust disclaimer 'HaqPath provides guidance based on published rules. Final eligibility is decided by the relevant authority.' is displayed on the results page whenever any result is shown.
triggers: The results page renders with at least one EligibilityResult
side_effects: The disclaimer appears prominently above or below the group list and is included in read-aloud output for the results
error_handling: If the results list is empty, the disclaimer still appears with the empty-state message

business_rules.name: results_recalculated_when_profile_changes
business_rules.description: Whenever a Profile answer that feeds any rule changes, the EligibilityResult records for that profile are recomputed and the results page reflects the new groups.
triggers: Lakshmi changes an answer, such as institution type, through the What changes my result interaction
Lakshmi returns to the results page after editing her profile
side_effects: Scheme cards move between groups to match the new profile
The card for any scheme whose status changed shows the rule that changed
error_handling: If recalculation fails, the page keeps the last valid results and shows a message that results may be out of date

business_rules.name: empty_group_shows_gentle_message
business_rules.description: When a result group has no schemes, its heading still appears with a short, calm message explaining that no schemes fall in that group for this profile.
triggers: The results page renders and a group has zero EligibilityResult records
side_effects: The family sees that the group was checked and is empty, rather than wondering whether the page failed
error_handling: If all three groups are empty, the page shows one general message suggesting the family review their answers

name: Scheme Detail Explains Why It Matched
description: Lakshmi opens a scheme from the results to see why it matched, what still needs checking, the documents, deadline, application steps, and official source, then saves it to her checklist.

steps.description: Lakshmi taps a scheme card in the Likely eligible or May qualify group.

business_rules.name: match_reasons_come_from_stored_rule_results
business_rules.description: The scheme detail screen shows the 'Why this may fit' reasons using the rule results already stored in EligibilityResult, without re-running matching or generating text with AI.
triggers: Lakshmi taps a scheme card in the Likely eligible or May qualify group on the results screen
side_effects: The scheme detail screen lists each matched EligibilityRule.plain_language_text under 'Why this may fit'
No new EligibilityResult is written when the detail screen opens
The 'Why this may fit' section is hidden if EligibilityResult.matched_rule_ids is empty
error_handling: If no EligibilityResult exists for the tapped Scheme and Profile, show a message that the result must be refreshed and send Lakshmi back to the results screen
If an EligibilityRule referenced in matched_rule_ids is missing, skip that reason and log the missing rule ID for the content team
If the stored result is older than the profile's latest answers, show the result with a notice that it may be out of date and offer to recalculate

business_rules.name: unverified_requirements_shown_as_next_steps
business_rules.description: Requirements that could not be confirmed from the profile are listed under 'What we still need to verify', so that 'May qualify' results clearly show what is still open.
triggers: Lakshmi opens a scheme detail for a result with status May qualify
Lakshmi opens a scheme detail for a Likely eligible result that still has unverified requirements
side_effects: The scheme detail screen lists each unverified requirement under 'What we still need to verify'
Each unverified requirement shows the plain-language question Lakshmi would need to confirm with the family or the school
error_handling: If unverified_rule_ids is empty for a May qualify result, show a generic note that the result depends on documents or details not yet confirmed and flag the data for review
If an EligibilityRule has no verification_question, show its plain_language_text without a question

business_rules.name: non_matching_reasons_shown_for_partial_results
business_rules.description: For May qualify results, the detail screen also explains which rules did not match in 'Why this may not fit', using failed rules stored in EligibilityResult.
triggers: Lakshmi opens a scheme detail for a May qualify result that has at least one failed rule
side_effects: The scheme detail screen lists each failed rule's plain-language reason under 'Why this may not fit'
Scheme.common_rejection_risks is shown as additional guidance beneath the failed reasons
error_handling: If failed_rule_ids is empty, hide the 'Why this may not fit' section instead of showing an empty heading
If Scheme.common_rejection_risks is empty, show only the failed rule reasons

business_rules.name: official_source_and_verification_date_always_shown
business_rules.description: Every scheme detail shows the official source link and the 'Last verified on' date from the Scheme record, placed prominently near the top of the screen.
triggers: Lakshmi opens any scheme detail screen
side_effects: The scheme detail screen shows 'Last verified on [Scheme.last_verified_at]' near the title
The official source link opens Scheme.official_url in a new browser tab
error_handling: If Scheme.official_url is missing, do not show the link and display a notice that the source is being verified, and flag the scheme for content review
If Scheme.last_verified_at is older than the allowed verification window, show the date with a warning that the scheme rules may have changed

business_rules.name: no_guaranteed_eligibility_language
business_rules.description: Scheme detail text uses only 'Likely eligible' and 'May qualify' wording and never states that the person is approved or guaranteed a benefit, taking the wording from Scheme.plain_language_explanation and EligibilityRule.plain_language_text.
triggers: Lakshmi opens any scheme detail screen
Any scheme detail content is loaded or rendered
side_effects: The status label on the detail screen reads 'Likely eligible' or 'May qualify' only
Any stored text containing words such as 'approved' or 'guaranteed' is blocked from display and flagged for content review
error_handling: If stored text contains a prohibited word, show the approved fallback wording 'Based on published rules, this scheme may suit you' and log the content record
If EligibilityResult.status is not one of the allowed values, do not render a status label and show a generic error

business_rules.name: disclaimer_shown_on_every_scheme_detail
business_rules.description: The scheme detail screen always displays the disclaimer 'HaqPath provides guidance based on published rules. Final eligibility is decided by the relevant authority.'
triggers: Lakshmi opens any scheme detail screen
side_effects: The disclaimer text appears at the bottom of the scheme detail, next to the 'How HaqPath decides' link
The disclaimer is included in the read-aloud text for the detail screen
error_handling: If the disclaimer component fails to load, the detail screen still renders with a fallback disclaimer line rather than leaving the disclaimer out

business_rules.name: scheme_detail_reads_without_profile_changes
business_rules.description: Opening a scheme detail is read-only: it never changes Profile answers, EligibilityResult values, or saved checklist progress.
triggers: Lakshmi opens and closes a scheme detail screen
side_effects: No Profile or EligibilityResult record is modified by opening the detail screen
Returning to the results screen shows the same grouping as before the detail was opened
error_handling: If a write is attempted during detail loading, cancel it and show the stored values

steps.description: The scheme detail shows Why this may fit, What we still need to verify, Why this may not fit, and Last verified on [date] with the official source link.

business_rules.name: scheme_detail_shows_stored_match_reasons
business_rules.description: The scheme detail page shows the reasons for the match exactly as the deterministic rule evaluation recorded them, never as generated AI text.
triggers: User taps a scheme card on the results screen
User opens a scheme detail link from a saved checklist
side_effects: The 'Why this may fit' section lists each rule the profile met, in plain language
Each reason is linked to the profile answer that satisfied it, such as the institution type or income band
error_handling: No EligibilityResult exists for this Scheme and Profile: show a message asking the user to answer the questions again, and do not show a made-up match
A matched rule has no plain_language_reason: show the rule's field and value in simple words and log the missing text for the data team

business_rules.name: unverified_conditions_listed_as_still_to_verify
business_rules.description: Every eligibility rule that could not be confirmed from the profile answers is listed under 'What we still need to verify', with the document or fact needed to confirm it.
triggers: Scheme detail page loads for a result with status 'May qualify'
Scheme detail page loads for a result where any rule was skipped or unanswered
side_effects: The 'What we still need to verify' section lists each unconfirmed condition in simple language
Each unconfirmed item points to the related document or fact the family should check
error_handling: Result status is 'Likely eligible' but unverified_items is not empty: downgrade the displayed status to 'May qualify' before rendering, since the status must match the open items
Unverified item has no matching required document: show the condition alone without a document reference

business_rules.name: failed_conditions_shown_respectfully_as_why_may_not_fit
business_rules.description: Every eligibility rule the profile failed is listed under 'Why this may not fit' using respectful, non-judgmental wording, and only when the scheme is not 'Likely eligible'.
triggers: Scheme detail page loads for a result with status 'May qualify' or 'Not currently eligible'
User changes a profile answer and the scheme detail page is reopened
side_effects: The 'Why this may not fit' section names each failed condition and the profile answer that caused it
The section is hidden for 'Likely eligible' results where no conditions failed
error_handling: Result is 'Likely eligible' but failed_reasons is not empty: treat it as a data error, hide the section, and log the inconsistency
Failed rule has no plain_language_reason: show a neutral fallback such as 'This condition is not met for the details you shared'

business_rules.name: scheme_detail_requires_official_source_and_verification_date
business_rules.description: A scheme detail page is only shown when the Scheme has an official_url and a last_verified_at date, and both are displayed prominently.
triggers: Scheme detail page loads for any Scheme
Results screen attempts to open a Scheme that has no verification record
side_effects: The page shows 'Last verified on [date]' near the top, above the explanation sections
The page shows a link to the official source, labelled with the scheme name
A scheme without an official_url or last_verified_at is removed from the results list
error_handling: Scheme.official_url is missing: block the detail page, show 'This scheme cannot be shown until its official source is confirmed', and exclude it from results
Scheme.last_verified_at is missing: block the detail page with the same approach
Scheme.official_url is malformed or does not start with https: block the page and log the record for correction

business_rules.name: detail_page_uses_only_approved_eligibility_wording
business_rules.description: The scheme detail page uses only the wording 'Likely eligible' or 'May qualify' for status, and always shows the disclaimer 'HaqPath provides guidance based on published rules. Final eligibility is decided by the relevant authority.'
triggers: Scheme detail page renders any EligibilityResult
Read-aloud button is used on the scheme detail page
side_effects: The status badge reads 'Likely eligible' or 'May qualify' (or 'Not currently eligible' for unavailable results)
The disclaimer appears at the bottom of the page and is included in read-aloud output
Any stored scheme text containing 'approved' or 'guaranteed' is replaced with the approved wording before display
error_handling: Scheme.plain_language_explanation contains 'approved' or 'guaranteed': hide that sentence, show the stored fallback text, and log the record for editing
Disclaimer text is missing from the page template: the page must not render and an error must be logged

business_rules.name: detail_page_shows_common_rejection_risks_and_deadline
business_rules.description: The scheme detail page shows the Scheme's common rejection risks and deadline so families know what commonly causes problems before they apply.
triggers: Scheme detail page loads for any Scheme with a deadline or rejection risk entries
side_effects: The deadline is shown with the number of days remaining
Each common rejection risk is listed in simple language under a 'Watch out for' heading
If the deadline has passed, the status shows 'Deadline passed' and the apply action is hidden
error_handling: Scheme.deadline is missing: show 'Deadline not published yet' and keep the rest of the page available
Scheme.common_rejection_risks is empty: hide the 'Watch out for' section rather than showing an empty heading

steps.description: Lakshmi taps the read-aloud button to hear the reasons and instructions in simple language.

business_rules.name: read_aloud_reads_full_scheme_explanation_in_order
business_rules.description: When the user taps read-aloud on a scheme detail screen, the button reads the scheme's content in this order: why it matched, what still needs verification, required documents, deadline, application steps, and official source.
triggers: User taps the ReadAloudButton on the Scheme detail screen
User taps the ReadAloudButton after changing a profile answer that updates the scheme's result
side_effects: Spoken output is generated for the current scheme and the current user's EligibilityResult
No record is changed; reading aloud is read-only
error_handling: If Scheme.plain_language_explanation is empty, read the structured fields (why matched, documents, deadline, steps) and skip the summary sentence
If the device has no speech output support, hide the ReadAloudButton and show the same text on screen
If the EligibilityResult for this scheme is missing, do not read a match reason; read only the scheme facts and say the user has not been checked yet

business_rules.name: read_aloud_speaks_stored_rules_not_generated_eligibility
business_rules.description: The read-aloud text is built from stored Scheme content and the deterministic EligibilityResult; AI may only rewrite the wording into simpler language and may never change whether the user is likely eligible, may qualify, or not currently eligible.
triggers: User taps the ReadAloudButton on the Scheme detail screen
Scheme.last_verified_at changes after a rule update
side_effects: A simple-language version of the stored explanation is generated through OpenAI and cached in Upstash keyed by Scheme.id, language, and Scheme.last_verified_at
The cached simple-language version is replaced when Scheme.last_verified_at changes
error_handling: If the OpenAI rewrite fails or times out, speak the stored Scheme.plain_language_explanation instead
If the rewritten text contains words that change the result (for example 'approved', 'guaranteed', or a status different from EligibilityResult.status), discard it and speak the stored text
If Upstash is unavailable, generate the rewrite again on request without caching

business_rules.name: read_aloud_always_includes_verification_date_and_disclaimer
business_rules.description: Every read-aloud session for a scheme ends by stating the Scheme.last_verified_at date and the disclaimer that HaqPath provides guidance based on published rules and the relevant authority decides final eligibility.
triggers: Read-aloud playback reaches the end of the scheme explanation
side_effects: The spoken closing statement gives the verification date and points the user to the official source link
error_handling: If Scheme.last_verified_at is missing, say that the date is not yet confirmed and do not read an old or guessed date
If playback is stopped early, the closing statement is not required to finish but is read first the next time the user starts playback

business_rules.name: read_aloud_uses_app_language_with_english_fallback
business_rules.description: Read-aloud speaks in the language the user has selected in the app (English or the regional language); if no regional-language explanation exists for a scheme, it speaks the English text.
triggers: User selects the regional language toggle on the Welcome screen or in the app header
User taps the ReadAloudButton
side_effects: The spoken language matches the chosen language for the whole scheme detail, including the verification and disclaimer statements
error_handling: If the device has no voice for the selected language, speak English and show a short note that the regional voice is not available
If Profile.preferred_language is not set, default to English

business_rules.name: read_aloud_can_be_paused_stopped_and_is_cancelled_on_leave
business_rules.description: Playback can be paused, resumed, or stopped by tapping the ReadAloudButton again, and it stops automatically when the user leaves the scheme detail screen or the app goes to the background.
triggers: User taps the ReadAloudButton while playback is running
User navigates away from the Scheme detail screen
The app moves to the background
side_effects: Speech output stops and the button returns to its ready state
No data is saved when playback stops
error_handling: If playback fails midway, reset the button and let the user start again from the beginning of the scheme

steps.description: Lakshmi taps Save to my checklist, which creates a personalised checklist for this scheme.

business_rules.name: one_checklist_per_profile_per_scheme
business_rules.description: A profile can hold only one checklist for a given scheme, so saving the same scheme again returns the existing checklist instead of creating a duplicate.
triggers: Lakshmi taps Save to my checklist on the scheme detail screen
Lakshmi taps Save to my checklist again after it has already been saved
side_effects: If no checklist exists for this profile and scheme, a new Checklist is created
If one already exists, the existing Checklist is shown and no new record is written
The button changes to Saved to my checklist with a link to the checklist
error_handling: If Lakshmi taps twice quickly, only one Checklist is written and both taps show the same result
If the save to the database fails, no partial Checklist is left behind and Lakshmi sees a message to try again

business_rules.name: checklist_created_with_status_not_started
business_rules.description: A new checklist always starts at Not started and moves forward in order only: Not started → Documents ready → Applied → Awaiting outcome.
triggers: A new Checklist is created from the save action
side_effects: Checklist.status is set to Not started
Checklist.created_at records the time of saving
The progress tracker shows this scheme at the first stage
error_handling: If a saved checklist somehow has no status, it is treated as Not started when displayed

business_rules.name: checklist_items_copied_from_scheme_documents_and_steps
business_rules.description: On save, each required document and each application step of the scheme is copied into the checklist as an unchecked item, plus one item for each eligibility requirement that still needs verification.
triggers: A new Checklist is created from the save action
side_effects: One ChecklistItem is created for each required document with item_type document and is_done set to false
One ChecklistItem is created for each application step with item_type step and is_done set to false
For a May qualify result, one ChecklistItem is created for each unverified requirement with item_type verify, so the family knows what to confirm
error_handling: If the scheme has no required documents listed, the checklist still saves with the application steps and a note that documents will be confirmed on the official site
If copying items fails partway, the whole checklist save is rolled back so the family never sees an incomplete checklist

business_rules.name: checklist_only_for_schemes_that_may_fit
business_rules.description: A checklist can be saved only for schemes whose EligibilityResult category is Likely eligible or May qualify, and the category at the time of saving is recorded on the checklist.
triggers: Lakshmi taps Save to my checklist on a scheme detail screen
side_effects: Checklist.eligibility_category stores Likely eligible or May qualify as shown at save time
For a Not currently eligible scheme, the save button is hidden and the screen explains that a checklist is only for schemes that may fit
error_handling: If the EligibilityResult has changed to Not currently eligible before saving, the save is refused and Lakshmi sees a message that the result has changed, with the new explanation
If no EligibilityResult exists for this profile and scheme, the save is refused and Lakshmi is asked to run the check again

business_rules.name: no_checklist_for_closed_deadline
business_rules.description: A checklist cannot be created for a scheme whose deadline has already passed, and the scheme's deadline is copied onto the checklist when it is saved.
triggers: Lakshmi taps Save to my checklist on a scheme whose deadline has passed
side_effects: If the deadline has not passed, the checklist is created with the scheme deadline shown in the countdown
If the deadline has passed, no Checklist is written and the screen shows that applications for this scheme are closed
error_handling: If the deadline is missing from the scheme data, the checklist is saved with a note that the deadline must be checked on the official site
If the deadline passes between opening the screen and tapping save, the save is refused with the closed message

business_rules.name: checklist_stores_profile_reference_only
business_rules.description: The checklist refers to the profile by its id only and stores no identity or sensitive details, so the saved list can be shared without exposing personal data.
triggers: A new Checklist is created from the save action
side_effects: Checklist holds only the profile id, the scheme id, the status, and the eligibility category
No copy of household income, class, or institution details is written onto the checklist itself
error_handling: If the profile id is missing or not found, the save is refused and Lakshmi is sent back to the intake screen to create a profile

name: What Changes My Result
description: Lakshmi changes one profile answer, such as institution type from government to private, and immediately sees which scheme result changes and which rule caused it.

steps.description: On the results screen Lakshmi taps What changes my result? and selects the institution type answer.

business_rules.name: institution_type_change_reevaluates_all_schemes
business_rules.description: When the profile's institution type changes, every scheme is re-checked against the deterministic eligibility rules so the results reflect the new answer immediately.
triggers: Lakshmi selects a different institution type in the What changes my result? panel on the results screen
side_effects: Profile.institution_type is saved with the newly selected value
An EligibilityResult is recalculated for each Scheme, with status set to likely, may_qualify, or not_currently_eligible
Results screen groups update to show which schemes moved between categories
error_handling: If a scheme's rules cannot be evaluated because a required rule is missing, its EligibilityResult is set to may_qualify with a note that the rule needs confirmation, and the failure is logged
If the save of the new Profile.institution_type fails, the previous value stays in place and the panel shows a retry message without changing any results

business_rules.name: changed_result_must_name_the_rule_that_flipped
business_rules.description: For each scheme whose status changed, the explanation lists the specific EligibilityRule whose outcome flipped between the previous and new institution type.
triggers: Recalculation finishes after an institution type change
Lakshmi opens the explanation for a scheme whose status changed
side_effects: The panel shows, for each changed scheme, the rule that changed (for example, the institution type rule for the scheme) and a plain-language reason
The previous and new EligibilityResult are stored together so the change can be shown again on the scheme detail screen
error_handling: If no single rule accounts for a status change, the panel says the result changed after several checks and lists each rule that differs
If a rule has no plain-language reason stored, the panel shows the rule's condition text instead of leaving the explanation blank

business_rules.name: skipped_institution_type_yields_may_qualify
business_rules.description: If the institution type is unanswered, any scheme that depends on it is shown as may_qualify with the institution type listed as something to verify, never as likely eligible.
triggers: Lakshmi clears or skips the institution type answer
Recalculation runs while Profile.institution_type is empty
side_effects: Affected EligibilityResult records are set to may_qualify
The results screen lists institution type under What we still need to verify for those schemes
error_handling: If every scheme depends on institution type, the panel shows a prompt asking Lakshmi to answer the question to see results

business_rules.name: checklist_progress_preserved_when_scheme_drops_out
business_rules.description: When a scheme moves to not_currently_eligible, its ChecklistItem records are kept with their progress status, marked as inactive, and are restored if the scheme becomes eligible again.
triggers: An institution type change moves a scheme to not_currently_eligible
A later institution type change moves that scheme back to likely or may_qualify
side_effects: ChecklistItem records for the affected scheme are marked inactive, with progress status unchanged
The active Checklist hides inactive items and shows a note that they were paused because the scheme no longer matches
Reactivated ChecklistItem records reappear with their previous progress
error_handling: If a ChecklistItem cannot be marked inactive, it stays visible and the panel notes that the checklist may need review

business_rules.name: result_change_wording_must_avoid_guarantees
business_rules.description: Text describing a changed result uses only the labels Likely eligible, May qualify, or Not currently eligible, and never uses words such as approved, guaranteed, or rejected.
triggers: Any recalculation that changes an EligibilityResult.status
side_effects: The panel and any explanation text show only approved status labels
The standard disclaimer is shown beneath the changed results
error_handling: If stored explanation text contains a prohibited word, that text is replaced with the approved status label and the content is flagged for editing

business_rules.name: institution_change_limited_to_demo_or_anonymous_profile
business_rules.description: The institution type change applies only to an anonymous or fictional demo Profile and does not collect or store identity details.
triggers: Lakshmi changes the institution type on the results screen
side_effects: Only Profile.institution_type and the derived EligibilityResult records are updated
No name, identity number, or bank detail is requested or stored
error_handling: If the profile is not anonymous or demo, the change is blocked and the user is told the panel works with sample profiles only

validation_rules.description: Institution type must be one of the allowed options: government, government_aided, or private.
validation_rules.error_message: Please choose the type of institution where your child studies.

steps.description: Lakshmi selects private as the new institution type, and the app re-evaluates the rules with the changed value.

business_rules.name: institution_type_change_reevaluates_all_schemes
business_rules.description: Whenever Profile.institution_type changes, every active Scheme is re-evaluated against its EligibilityRule set in the same interaction, so results never reflect a previous institution type.
triggers: Lakshmi selects a new institution type (government, government_aided, or private) on the profile step
The useEligibility hook receives a changed Profile.institution_type value
side_effects: Profile.institution_type is saved with the new value
A new EligibilityResult is computed for each Scheme with status set to Likely eligible, May qualify, or Not currently eligible
The results screen updates immediately to show the recomputed groups
error_handling: If a Scheme has no EligibilityRule data, it is excluded from re-evaluation and shown with a 'Rules being updated' note rather than being marked eligible or ineligible
If re-evaluation fails, the previous EligibilityResult set is kept and the user sees a message asking them to try again

business_rules.name: institution_type_mismatch_moves_scheme_to_not_currently_eligible
business_rules.description: When Profile.institution_type is not in EligibilityRule.institution_types for a Scheme, that Scheme's EligibilityResult moves to Not currently eligible, with the failed institution rule named as the reason (for example, government_aided-only schemes when the profile is private).
triggers: Profile.institution_type is changed to a value outside a Scheme's EligibilityRule.institution_types list
side_effects: The Scheme appears under Not currently eligible with a respectful explanation such as 'This scheme is for government and government-aided institutions'
The 'Why this may not fit' text on the scheme detail is updated to name the institution rule
error_handling: If the institution rule is missing for a Scheme, the Scheme is not moved to Not currently eligible and is flagged for review instead

business_rules.name: institution_type_change_records_which_rule_changed
business_rules.description: The system compares the previous and new EligibilityResult for each Scheme and records the specific EligibilityRule that caused each status change, so the 'What changes my result?' view can show it.
triggers: Profile.institution_type changes and the recomputed EligibilityResult differs from the previous one
side_effects: Each changed Scheme shows an entry such as 'Changed from Likely eligible to Not currently eligible because institution type is now private'
Unchanged Schemes show no change entry
error_handling: If no rule can be identified as the cause of a change, the entry says 'Result changed after your answers were updated' and the changed rule is logged for review

business_rules.name: saved_checklist_flagged_not_deleted_on_result_change
business_rules.description: If a Scheme with a saved Checklist moves to Not currently eligible after an institution type change, the Checklist and its ChecklistItem records are kept and flagged for review, not deleted.
triggers: A Scheme with an existing Checklist changes to Not currently eligible after Profile.institution_type changes
side_effects: The Checklist for that Scheme shows a notice that the result has changed and progress is kept
ChecklistItem.status values are unchanged
error_handling: If the Checklist cannot be flagged, the change is still saved and the user sees the saved checklist without a notice, with the error logged

business_rules.name: result_wording_never_guarantees_eligibility
business_rules.description: Every EligibilityResult shown after an institution type change uses only the status labels Likely eligible, May qualify, or Not currently eligible, and never says approved or guaranteed.
triggers: A recomputed EligibilityResult is rendered on the results or scheme detail screen
side_effects: Status labels and change messages use approved trust-layer wording
The disclaimer 'HaqPath provides guidance based on published rules. Final eligibility is decided by the relevant authority.' remains visible on the results screen
error_handling: If generated explanation text contains prohibited words such as approved or guaranteed, it is replaced with the rule-based template text and the event is logged

validation_rules.description: An institution type must be selected before results are recomputed.
validation_rules.error_message: Please choose your child's institution type to see your results.

validation_rules.description: Institution type must be one of government, government_aided, or private, matching the values used in EligibilityRule.institution_types.
validation_rules.error_message: Please choose one of the listed institution types.

steps.description: The results update to show the scheme that no longer matches, with the rule that changed (institution_types now excludes private).

business_rules.name: institution_change_reevaluates_all_schemes
business_rules.description: When the institution type in the Profile changes, every Scheme is re-checked against its EligibilityRule set, and each EligibilityResult is recalculated from scratch with no AI involvement.
triggers: User changes Profile.institution_type on the results page (for example, from government to private)
User selects a different institution type in the 'What changes my result?' control
side_effects: EligibilityResult.status is recalculated for every Scheme in the catalogue
EligibilityResult.previous_status keeps the status shown before the change so the difference can be displayed
The results page regroups schemes into Likely eligible, May qualify, and Not currently eligible without a page reload
error_handling: If Profile.institution_type is cleared or unset, the Profile is treated as incomplete and schemes that depend on institution type move to May qualify with the missing detail flagged, not to Not currently eligible
If an EligibilityRule cannot be loaded from Upstash, the previous EligibilityResult is kept and the page shows that results could not be refreshed, instead of showing a guessed status

business_rules.name: institution_types_rule_excludes_private_institutions
business_rules.description: A Scheme whose EligibilityRule lists institution_types as government and government_aided does not match a Profile whose institution_type is private, so its EligibilityResult moves from Likely eligible to Not currently eligible.
triggers: Profile.institution_type is set or changed to private
Scheme evaluation runs against a Profile with a private institution
side_effects: EligibilityResult.status becomes not_eligible for the affected Scheme
EligibilityResult.failed_rule records institution_types as the rule that failed
The Scheme card shows the plain-language reason that the institution type no longer fits, along with the rule that changed
error_handling: If the EligibilityRule for the Scheme has no institution_types list, this rule is skipped and the Scheme is not marked not_eligible on this basis
If the Profile institution type is unknown, the rule returns unconfirmed rather than failed, so the Scheme is shown under May qualify

business_rules.name: result_change_explains_the_rule_that_changed
business_rules.description: When a Scheme's EligibilityResult status changes after a Profile edit, the system stores which EligibilityRule field changed and the old and new values, so the change can be explained in plain language.
triggers: EligibilityResult.status differs from the previous value after recalculation
User opens the 'What changes my result?' explanation for a Scheme
side_effects: EligibilityResult.changed_rule is set to the rule field that caused the difference (for example, institution_types)

The results page displays a message stating the old value, the new value, and the rule that changed, for example: 'Government-aided and government institutions only. Your institution is now private, so this scheme no longer matches.'
The change message is read out when read-aloud is used
error_handling: If the status did not change, no change message is shown for that Scheme
If more than one rule changed, all changed rule fields are listed in the explanation, in the order they are evaluated

validation_rules.description: An institution type must be selected before the results can be recalculated.
validation_rules.error_message: Please choose the type of school or college your child attends.

validation_rules.description: The institution type must be one of the allowed values: government, government_aided, or private.
validation_rules.error_message: Please pick one of the options shown: government, government-aided, or private.

name: Document Checklist and Application Steps
description: Lakshmi reviews the personalised documents and step-by-step application guide for a scheme, ticks off completed items, and shares a privacy-safe text summary with family.

steps.description: Lakshmi opens the checklist from her saved scheme, which lists the required documents and application steps.

business_rules.name: checklist_items_come_from_scheme_required_documents
business_rules.description: Each Checklist shows exactly the documents listed in its Scheme's required_documents, one ChecklistItem per document, in the order the scheme lists them.
triggers: Lakshmi opens the checklist from her saved scheme
The checklist is opened for the first time for a saved scheme
side_effects: ChecklistItem records are created for each required document of the scheme, all starting unchecked
The checklist screen lists each required document as a ChecklistItem
error_handling: If the scheme has no required_documents, the checklist shows a plain message that the scheme's document list is still being confirmed and links to the official source
If the Scheme record cannot be found, the checklist does not open and Lakshmi is returned to her saved schemes with a message that the scheme is no longer available

business_rules.name: application_steps_follow_scheme_published_order
business_rules.description: The step-by-step application guide shows the Scheme's application_steps in the exact order published, without reordering or rewording the official sequence beyond plain-language simplification.
triggers: Lakshmi opens the application steps section of the checklist
side_effects: The application guide displays the scheme's steps as a numbered sequence on the checklist screen
error_handling: If application_steps is empty, the guide shows a message that steps are not yet published and directs Lakshmi to the official source
If a step references an action outside HaqPath, the step is shown as text only and HaqPath does not submit anything on her behalf

business_rules.name: official_source_and_verification_date_shown_with_checklist
business_rules.description: Every checklist displays the Scheme's official_url as the official source and the Scheme's last_verified_at date prominently, alongside the required documents and steps.
triggers: Lakshmi opens any checklist
Lakshmi taps the official source link on the checklist
side_effects: The checklist shows a 'Last verified on [date]' label and an official source link
Tapping the official source opens the government page in a new view
error_handling: If official_url is missing, the checklist does not display as verified and shows that the official source is being confirmed
If last_verified_at is older than the stated freshness window, the checklist still shows the date with a note asking Lakshmi to confirm on the official site

business_rules.name: deadline_shown_on_checklist
business_rules.description: The checklist displays the Scheme's deadline so Lakshmi can see how much time remains to apply.
triggers: Lakshmi opens a checklist
side_effects: The checklist shows the scheme deadline and the number of days remaining
error_handling: If deadline is missing, the checklist shows 'Deadline not yet announced' and points to the official source
If the deadline has passed, the checklist shows that the application window has closed and does not offer a step to mark the scheme as applied

business_rules.name: opening_checklist_does_not_change_progress_status
business_rules.description: Opening a checklist leaves Checklist.status unchanged; progress moves only through the sequence Not started → Documents ready → Applied → Awaiting outcome when Lakshmi explicitly updates it.
triggers: Lakshmi opens the checklist without changing any item
side_effects: Checklist.status is shown as it currently is, with no automatic advancement
error_handling: If a stored Checklist.status is not one of the four allowed values, the checklist shows as 'Not started' and the invalid value is not displayed to Lakshmi

business_rules.name: checklist_remains_linked_to_eligibility_result
business_rules.description: The checklist shows the current EligibilityResult category for its Scheme, so if a profile change alters the result, the checklist shows the updated category with a short reason.
triggers: Lakshmi opens a checklist after changing a profile answer
The eligibility result for the saved scheme is recalculated
side_effects: The checklist header shows the scheme's current category (Likely eligible, May qualify, or Not currently eligible)
The checklist shows the rule that changed when the category is no longer Likely eligible
error_handling: If no EligibilityResult exists for the scheme, the checklist shows 'Eligibility being checked' and does not show a category
If the result is Not currently eligible, the checklist still opens for reference but states that the scheme may not fit the current profile

steps.description: Lakshmi ticks each document as ready and each application step as done.

business_rules.name: tick_marks_checklist_item_done
business_rules.description: Ticking a document or application step sets that ChecklistItem to done, and unticking it sets it back to not done.
triggers: Lakshmi ticks a document as ready
Lakshmi ticks an application step as done
Lakshmi unticks a previously ticked item
side_effects: ChecklistItem.is_done becomes true, and ChecklistItem.completed_at is recorded, when ticked
ChecklistItem.is_done becomes false and ChecklistItem.completed_at is cleared when unticked
the item's new state is saved so it is still shown after a page reload
error_handling: If the save fails, the tick reverts to its previous state and a short message asks Lakshmi to try again
If the device is offline, the tick is shown immediately and saved when the connection returns
If the ChecklistItem no longer exists, the list refreshes and a message says the item was removed

business_rules.name: checklist_status_follows_ticks
business_rules.description: Checklist.status moves through Not started → Documents ready → Applied → Awaiting outcome, and moves to Documents ready only when every document item is ticked and to Applied only when every application step item is ticked.
triggers: A ChecklistItem is ticked or unticked
The last document item is ticked
The last application step item is ticked
side_effects: Checklist.status becomes Documents ready when all document items are done
Checklist.status becomes Applied when all application step items are done
Checklist.status falls back to Not started or Documents ready when items are unticked
the progress tracker shows the new status for this scheme
error_handling: If a checklist has no document items, Documents ready is not reached and the status stays Not started until application steps are done
If the status cannot be saved, the previous status is shown and the tick is retried

business_rules.name: ticks_are_self_declared_not_verified
business_rules.description: A document tick records only that the user says the document is ready; HaqPath does not check, store, or verify the document, and an application step tick does not submit anything to a government portal.
triggers: Lakshmi ticks a document as ready
Lakshmi ticks an application step as done
side_effects: the item is marked done with no file attached and no data sent to any authority
the checklist page shows a note that ticks are for personal tracking only
error_handling: No error is raised for a self-declared tick, since no document content is requested

business_rules.name: ticks_do_not_change_eligibility
business_rules.description: Ticking checklist items never changes the EligibilityResult or the EligibilityRule evaluation for the scheme.
triggers: Lakshmi ticks or unticks any ChecklistItem
side_effects: the EligibilityResult for the scheme stays the same after any tick
the results screen still shows the original match category
error_handling: If an eligibility change is somehow triggered by a tick, the change is discarded and the original EligibilityResult is kept

business_rules.name: checklist_items_belong_to_one_scheme_checklist
business_rules.description: Each ChecklistItem belongs to exactly one Checklist, and each Checklist belongs to exactly one Scheme, so ticks on one scheme never change another scheme's items.
triggers: Lakshmi opens a scheme's checklist and ticks an item
side_effects: only the ticked item in the open Checklist is updated
other schemes' checklists and their Checklist.status values are unchanged
error_handling: If a tick references an item from a different Checklist, the request is rejected and the list is reloaded

validation_rules.description: Each tick must send a true or false value for the item's done state.
validation_rules.error_message: We could not update this item. Please try ticking it again.

validation_rules.description: Each tick must refer to an item whose type is either document or application step, so the status rules can count each group correctly.
validation_rules.error_message: This item could not be recognised. Please refresh the checklist and try again.

steps.description: Lakshmi taps Share this checklist with family and gets a short text summary with scheme names, document names, and deadlines but no sensitive identity or income details.

business_rules.name: share_summary_excludes_sensitive_details
business_rules.description: The shared summary includes only scheme names, document names, and deadlines, and never includes income, identity numbers, or other personal profile details.
